tasks.title: Assert Dispatcher's CancellationToken propagation and its missing-handler failure mode (MASTER-172, MASTER-173)
acceptance: A1. NEW FILE src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Dispatch/DispatcherCancellationTests.cs declares public class DispatcherCancellationTests in namespace DungeonMaster.Tests.Application.Common.Dispatch, and contains a [Fact] named SendAsync_WithAToken_PassesThatSameTokenToTheCommandHandler which dispatches a test-local ICommand through an IDispatcher resolved from a ServiceCollection-built provider (no IPipelineBehavior registered), passing a token whose value differs from CancellationToken.None, and asserts that the CancellationToken the command handler received equals that same token. (The repository's idiom for producing such a token is a CancellationTokenSource, src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Handlers/CommandHandlerTestBase.cs:72; the idiom is cited, not mandated.) Falsifiable by: dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DispatcherCancellationTests.SendAsync_WithAToken_PassesThatSameTokenToTheCommandHandler" -- reports Passed: 1, Failed: 0.

A2. Falsifiable by the same dotnet test command with --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DispatcherCancellationTests.SendAsyncOfT_WithAToken_PassesThatSameTokenToTheCommandHandler" -- Passed: 1, Failed: 0.

A10. INJECTION ROUND A (handler hand-off). With the three handler hand-off arguments in src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Dispatch/Dispatcher.cs temporarily replaced -- the `ct` argument of `handler.HandleAsync(typed, ct)` at :139, :172 and :205 replaced by `new CancellationToken(false)`, leaving the `ct` passed to BuildPipeline at :140, :173 and :206 untouched -- the command `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Application.Common.Dispatch"` builds with exit code 0 on the build and reports exactly these three tests failed: the A1, A2 and A3 facts; and reports the A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 facts and all six [Fact] of DispatcherTests passing. The edit is reverted afterwards (see A14). `new CancellationToken(false)` is specified rather than `default` or `CancellationToken.None` so that CA2016 (forward the CancellationToken parameter) cannot convert this injection into a build failure under TreatWarningsAsErrors.

A11. INJECTION ROUND B (pipeline hand-off). With the three pipeline hand-off arguments in Dispatcher.cs temporarily replaced -- the final `ct` argument of the BuildPipeline call at :140, :173 and :206 replaced by `new CancellationToken(false)`, leaving the `ct` handed to the handler at :139, :172 and :205 untouched -- the same filtered dotnet test command reports exactly these three tests failed: the A4, A5 and A6 facts; and reports the A1, A2, A3, A7, A8, A9 facts and all six [Fact] of DispatcherTests passing. The edit is reverted afterwards (see A14).

A12. INJECTION ROUND C (handler resolution). With the three resolution sites in Dispatcher.cs temporarily replaced -- `GetRequiredService<...>()` at :131, :164 and :197 replaced by `GetService<...>()!` (the null-forgiving operator is required, or CS8602 fails the build under TreatWarningsAsErrors) -- the same filtered dotnet test command reports exactly these three tests failed: the A7, A8 and A9 facts; and reports the A1 through A6 facts and all six [Fact] of DispatcherTests passing. The edit is reverted afterwards (see A14).

This file is listed in `owns` solely so the temporary injections in A10-A12 are legal; no permanent production change is in scope for this session.

A15. [AMENDED A1, escalation E1.] Every [Fact] method in the two new files, and every type declared in them that carries neither type parameters nor primary-constructor parameters, is immediately preceded by an XML doc comment ending in `/// </summary>`. Every remaining declared type -- those carrying <typeparam> or <param> documentation -- is preceded by an XML doc comment that OPENS with a `/// <summary>` block, which is the repository's actual convention: under it the last line before such a declaration is `</typeparam>` or `</param>`, not `</summary>`. Measured this session across the three test projects: 20 type declarations are immediately preceded by `</typeparam>` or `</param>` across 13 files, 16 of them pre-existing, including DispatcherTests.cs:231-243 -- the very declaration this criterion originally cited as its convention. Falsifiable by: grep -n -B1 "\[Fact\]" <each new file> -- every line printed immediately above a [Fact] line is a `/// </summary>` line, with no [Fact] lacking one.

A16. The full test project is green with the new files in place and Dispatcher.cs restored: dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj reports Failed: 0 and exits 0 (TreatWarningsAsErrors=true in Directory.Build.props:5 with EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true at :16 means any formatting or analyser slip in the new files fails this command rather than warning).
